title: Where do we land if we step back four sevenths from six sevenths?
description: A number line from zero to one is cut into seven equal steps. We start at six sevenths and jump four steps of one seventh to the left, and the dot stops where the answer is. Keeko's doubt is that the mark we stand on counts as the first jump.
teaching_notes: One idea: taking away on the number line means jumping left over equal steps, and the jumps are counted by the steps crossed. Watch for students who count the starting mark as a jump.

source: Try doing 6/7 − 4/7 using the number line.
video_script.why: The child sees the same take away as movement to the left on a number line, so the answer from the strip is checked in a second picture.
video_script.substitution: The book's number line from zero to one cut into seven equal steps, each step one seventh.
video_script.anchor: the number line from zero to one cut into seven equal steps, with a dot that starts at six sevenths
video_script.wrong_answer: the mark we stand on counts as the first jump
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts the mark where the dot stands as jump one, so only three steps are crossed and the dot stops one step too early.
video_script.payoff_line: Six sevenths take away four sevenths lands on two sevenths
video_script.fraction_reading: one seventh, three sevenths, four sevenths, five sevenths, six sevenths, two sevenths
never_show: the label 2/7 on the number line before the answer beat
maths_rules: the number line from 0 to 1 is cut into 7 equal steps, each step is 1/7
the dot starts at 6/7, the sixth mark after 0
taking away 4/7 is 4 jumps of 1/7 to the left
the jumps pass 5/7, 4/7 and 3/7 and the fourth jump lands at 2/7
6 − 4 = 2, so the dot is 2 steps of 1/7 from 0
6/7 − 4/7 = 2/7, the same as on the strip
Keeko's slip: counting the standing mark as jump 1 gives only 3 steps crossed and lands on 3/7
video_script.design: One number line, one dot. Jumps are counted by the steps crossed. Only 0, 6/7 and 1 are labelled until the walk begins.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a number line from 0 to 1 cut into 7 equal steps with only 0, 6/7 and 1 labelled; a dot sits at 6/7

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.line: the number line from 0 to 1 appears cut into 7 equal steps
marks.ask: the dot at 6/7 glows and an arrow of 4 steps points left

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about taking away fractions on the number line.
<bookmark mark='line'/>The line from zero to one is cut into seven equal steps.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We start at six sevenths and move four steps back to the left. Where do we land?

beats.on_screen: the number line holds still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the number line with each step marked 1/7; an arrow pointing left with the words take away means move left

marks.unit: one step lights up and is marked 1/7
marks.mark: the dot glows at the sixth mark after 0

narration: <bookmark mark='unit'/>Each step on the line is one seventh. This size of step is called the fractional unit.
<bookmark mark='mark'/>Six sevenths is the mark after six steps from zero.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Taking away means moving to the left, towards zero.

beats.on_screen: Given: number line 0 to 1 in 7 equal steps; start at 6/7

marks.given: the start 6/7 and the seven steps are written on the working board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the line from zero to one has seven equal steps, and we start at six sevenths.

beats.on_screen: To find: where we land after taking away 4/7, that is 6/7 − 4/7

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find where we land after taking away four sevenths.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: put the dot at 6/7, the 6th mark after 0

marks.start: the dot is placed at 6/7 and the 6 steps from 0 are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='start'/>Step one, put the dot at six sevenths, because that is where we start.
It is the sixth mark after zero.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: jump 4 steps of 1/7 to the left; the dot passes 5/7, 4/7 and 3/7 and makes a 4th jump

marks.jump: four jump arcs of one step each appear from the dot towards the left
marks.pass: the labels 5/7, 4/7 and 3/7 appear under the marks the dot passes
marks.last: the fourth jump arc glows and the dot lands, its mark left unlabelled

narration: <bookmark mark='jump'/>Step two, jump four steps of one seventh to the left, because we take away four sevenths.
<bookmark mark='pass'/>The jumps pass five sevenths, four sevenths and three sevenths.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last jump brings the dot to its new place.

marks.count: the steps between 0 and the dot are counted, 2 of them

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step three, count the steps from zero to the dot.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Six take away four leaves two steps, and each step is one seventh.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 6/7 − 4/7 lands on 2/7 on the number line

marks.ans: the label 2/7 appears under the dot and is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Six sevenths take away four sevenths lands on two sevenths on the number line.
It is the same answer as on the strip.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: the standing mark counted as jump 1, so only 3 steps are crossed and the dot stops on 3/7; the bubble is struck through; the 4 real jumps return

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows the standing mark numbered as jump 1
marks.gap: one step between two marks glows as a jump
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the dot jumps from 6/7 to 5/7

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the mark we stand on counts as the first jump.
Then four jumps would stop on three sevenths.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>But a jump crosses one whole step between two marks.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Standing still crosses nothing. The first jump goes from six sevenths to five sevenths.
We count the steps crossed, never the marks.
